headline: A Thanksgiving storm brings heavy rain, possible flash flooding in New York City, gusts up to about 60 mph across the city and Long Island Thursday afternoon and evening, and widespread moderate coastal flooding at both Thursday high tides.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: High pressure keeps Wednesday dry around New York City as it slides by to the north, with light east-northeast winds. Low clouds move into the city and south shore after about 1 AM Thursday, and winds pick up toward the Thursday morning commute. Minor coastal flooding is expected with Wednesday morning's high tide in southern Nassau County.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The Thanksgiving storm is on track, with the worst rain and wind most likely Thursday afternoon and evening within a window of roughly 10 AM to the overnight hours. A High Wind Warning runs 10 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday for New York City, Long Island and nearby northeast New Jersey, with gusts up to about 60 mph, while a Wind Advisory covers inland northeast New Jersey (now including western Passaic County), the nearby lower Hudson Valley and southern Connecticut from 10 AM Thursday to 5 AM Friday with 45 to 55 mph gusts. Rain totals have been raised; the heaviest falls Thursday evening with a possible rumble of thunder and a slight chance of 1-inch-per-hour downpours near New York City, which is at a Slight Risk for flash flooding (Marginal Risk elsewhere, where minor poor-drainage flooding is more likely). Drier air cuts the rain off Thursday evening, leaving light rain or drizzle overnight into Friday morning, then a few light showers Friday afternoon with west winds gusting to roughly 30 to 40 mph.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday stays breezy with west winds gusting to roughly 25 to 35 mph and possibly some low clouds. Sunday looks calmer with light southwest winds and generally good conditions. The discussion gives no temperature details or specifics beyond the weekend.

coast: Strong east-northeast gale- to storm-force winds Thursday morning into Thursday night bring widespread moderate coastal flooding at both the Thursday morning and evening high tides, with a chance of major flooding along the western Great South Bay and significant impacts around Peconic Bay and the Peconic River and along the western Long Island Sound shoreline; surge up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers brings minor to moderate flooding. Thursday morning's tide is naturally higher, but the peak surge arrives Thursday afternoon and evening, so both tides may reach similar levels, and heavy rain during the evening tide could worsen coastal street flooding. A Coastal Flood Warning runs 7 AM Thursday to 6 AM Friday for the whole coastline except southeastern Connecticut (under an advisory through 3 PM Friday), and a Coastal Flood Watch covers Friday's daytime high tide, when southwest winds may bring another round of moderate flooding to the southern bays of Long Island and Queens, especially the eastern Great South Bay, with minor flooding elsewhere. On the ocean beaches 8 to 12 foot breakers bring widespread beach flooding, dune erosion and possible localized overwash, while western Long Island Sound and the Twin Forks see 3 to 6 foot waves with dune erosion, splashover and possible isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. A Gale Warning (6 PM Wednesday to 6 AM Thursday) gives way to a Storm Warning on all waters from 6 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday, with ocean seas near 20 feet late Thursday afternoon and evening and waves up to about 10 feet on the Sound and at the New York Harbor entrance; a southwest gale is likely on the ocean Friday, easing to small-craft levels Saturday and below that Sunday.

Downpours and possible flash flooding in New York City Thursday evening, especially coinciding with high tide
Water levels at Thursday's morning and evening high tides
confidence: Confidence is high that the storm will hit Thursday, but models still differ on timing, and the coastal flood forecast leans toward the higher end of possibilities for a safety margin; little detail is given beyond the weekend.
